1Easy

Define fff on [0,1][0,1][0,1] by f(1/2)=1f(1/2) = 1f(1/2)=1 and f(x)=0f(x) = 0f(x)=0 for x≠1/2x \ne 1/2x=1/2.

Prove directly from upper and lower sums that fff is Riemann integrable with ∫01f=0\int_0^1 f = 0∫01​f=0.

  • Upper and Lower Sums Close In
Show solution

  1. The function fff is bounded (0≤f≤10 \le f \le 10≤f≤1). For 0<δ<1/20 < \delta < 1/20<δ<1/2 take the partition Pδ={0, 1/2−δ, 1/2+δ, 1}P_\delta = \{0,\ 1/2 - \delta,\ 1/2 + \delta,\ 1\}Pδ​={0, 1/2−δ, 1/2+δ, 1}.

    On the two outer intervals f≡0f \equiv 0f≡0, so both the infimum and supremum are 000; on the middle interval [1/2−δ, 1/2+δ][1/2-\delta,\ 1/2+\delta][1/2−δ, 1/2+δ] the infimum is 000 (points other than 1/21/21/2 exist) and the supremum is 111 (since f(1/2)=1f(1/2) = 1f(1/2)=1).

  2. Hence the lower sum is L(Pδ,f)=0L(P_\delta, f) = 0L(Pδ​,f)=0 and the upper sum is U(Pδ,f)=1⋅2δ=2δU(P_\delta, f) = 1 \cdot 2\delta = 2\deltaU(Pδ​,f)=1⋅2δ=2δ. Since U−L=2δ→0U - L = 2\delta \to 0U−L=2δ→0 as δ→0+\delta \to 0^+δ→0+, the Riemann criterion gives integrability.

    The integral satisfies 0=L(Pδ,f)≤∫01f≤U(Pδ,f)=2δ0 = L(P_\delta, f) \le \int_0^1 f \le U(P_\delta, f) = 2\delta0=L(Pδ​,f)≤∫01​f≤U(Pδ​,f)=2δ for every δ>0\delta > 0δ>0, so it equals 000 — the value at a single point does not affect the Riemann integral.

Show solution

  1. Get F′(0)F'(0)F′(0) from the definition: F(h)−F(0)h=hsin⁡(1/h2)\dfrac{F(h) - F(0)}{h} = h\sin(1/h^2)hF(h)−F(0)​=hsin(1/h2), and ∣hsin⁡(1/h2)∣≤∣h∣\lvert h\sin(1/h^2) \rvert \le \lvert h \rvert∣hsin(1/h2)∣≤∣h∣, so the squeeze theorem gives the limit 000.

    For x≠0x \ne 0x=0, the product and chain rules give F′(x)=2xsin⁡(1/x2)+x2cos⁡(1/x2)⋅(−2/x3)=2xsin⁡(1/x2)−2xcos⁡(1/x2)F'(x) = 2x\sin(1/x^2) + x^2\cos(1/x^2)\cdot(-2/x^3) = 2x\sin(1/x^2) - \dfrac{2}{x}\cos(1/x^2)F′(x)=2xsin(1/x2)+x2cos(1/x2)⋅(−2/x3)=2xsin(1/x2)−x2​cos(1/x2). Hence FFF is differentiable at every point of [−1,1][-1,1][−1,1].

  2. But F′F'F′ is unbounded near 000.

    Put xk=12πk→0+x_k = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi k}} \to 0^+xk​=2πk​1​→0+ (k=1,2,…k = 1, 2, \dotsk=1,2,…): then sin⁡(1/xk2)=sin⁡(2πk)=0\sin(1/x_k^2) = \sin(2\pi k) = 0sin(1/xk2​)=sin(2πk)=0 and cos⁡(1/xk2)=cos⁡(2πk)=1\cos(1/x_k^2) = \cos(2\pi k) = 1cos(1/xk2​)=cos(2πk)=1, so F′(xk)=−2xk=−22πk→−∞F'(x_k) = -\dfrac{2}{x_k} = -2\sqrt{2\pi k} \to -\inftyF′(xk​)=−xk​2​=−22πk​→−∞. Every neighborhood of 000 contains xkx_kxk​ for large kkk, so F′F'F′ is unbounded there.

  3. A Riemann integrable function must be bounded (needed for finite upper sums), so F′F'F′ is not Riemann integrable on [−1,1][-1,1][−1,1].

    FTC-II asserts "∫abF′=F(b)−F(a)\int_a^b F' = F(b) - F(a)∫ab​F′=F(b)−F(a)" but requires F′F'F′ to be Riemann integrable as a hypothesis — this example shows that without it the integral ∫−11F′\int_{-1}^{1} F'∫−11​F′ does not even exist, so the theorem cannot be applied. Differentiability alone is not enough.

3Medium

Let fff and ggg be of bounded variation on [a,b][a,b][a,b].

First show a BV function is bounded (hint: ∣f(x)−f(a)∣≤Vab(f)\lvert f(x) - f(a) \rvert \le V_a^b(f)∣f(x)−f(a)∣≤Vab​(f)), then prove the product fgfgfg is also of bounded variation on [a,b][a,b][a,b]. Find an upper bound for its total variation.

Vab(fg)≤Mf Vab(g)+Mg Vab(f),Mf=sup⁡[a,b]∣f∣, Mg=sup⁡[a,b]∣g∣V_a^b(fg) \le M_f\,V_a^b(g) + M_g\,V_a^b(f), \qquad M_f = \sup_{[a,b]}\lvert f \rvert,\ M_g = \sup_{[a,b]}\lvert g \rvertVab​(fg)≤Mf​Vab​(g)+Mg​Vab​(f),Mf​=[a,b]sup​∣f∣, Mg​=[a,b]sup​∣g∣
  • Functions of Bounded Variation
Show solution

  1. For x∈[a,b]x \in [a,b]x∈[a,b], the partition {a,x,b}\{a, x, b\}{a,x,b} gives ∣f(x)−f(a)∣≤Vab(f)\lvert f(x) - f(a) \rvert \le V_a^b(f)∣f(x)−f(a)∣≤Vab​(f), so by the triangle inequality ∣f(x)∣≤∣f(a)∣+Vab(f)<∞\lvert f(x) \rvert \le \lvert f(a) \rvert + V_a^b(f) < \infty∣f(x)∣≤∣f(a)∣+Vab​(f)<∞. Hence fff is bounded with Mf=sup⁡[a,b]∣f∣<∞M_f = \sup_{[a,b]}\lvert f \rvert < \inftyMf​=sup[a,b]​∣f∣<∞, and likewise for ggg.

  2. For any partition P={x0,…,xn}P = \{x_0, \dots, x_n\}P={x0​,…,xn​}, use the identity f(xi)g(xi)−f(xi−1)g(xi−1)=f(xi)(g(xi)−g(xi−1))+g(xi−1)(f(xi)−f(xi−1))f(x_i)g(x_i) - f(x_{i-1})g(x_{i-1}) = f(x_i)\bigl(g(x_i) - g(x_{i-1})\bigr) + g(x_{i-1})\bigl(f(x_i) - f(x_{i-1})\bigr)f(xi​)g(xi​)−f(xi−1​)g(xi−1​)=f(xi​)(g(xi​)−g(xi−1​))+g(xi−1​)(f(xi​)−f(xi−1​)).

    Taking absolute values and summing, \[\sum_{i=1}^{n}\lvert (fg)(x_i) - (fg)(x_{i-1}) \rvert \le M_f \sum_{i=1}^{n}\lvert g(x_i) - g(x_{i-1}) \rvert + M_g \sum_{i=1}^{n}\lvert f(x_i) - f(x_{i-1}) \rvert \le M_f V_a^b(g) + M_g V_a^b(f).\] The right side is independent of PPP, so taking the supremum gives Vab(fg)≤MfVab(g)+MgVab(f)<∞V_a^b(fg) \le M_f V_a^b(g) + M_g V_a^b(f) < \inftyVab​(fg)≤Mf​Vab​(g)+Mg​Vab​(f)<∞: fgfgfg is of bounded variation.

4HardCounterexample

The uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous (the Weierstrass scene).

Show this fails for bounded variation: with g(x)=x2sin⁡(1/x2)g(x) = x^2\sin(1/x^2)g(x)=x2sin(1/x2) for x>0x > 0x>0 and g(0)=0g(0) = 0g(0)=0, put \[g_n(x) = \begin{cases} g(1/n) & 0 \le x \le 1/n \\ g(x) & 1/n \le x \le 1 \end{cases}.\]

(a) Show ggg is NOT of bounded variation on [0,1][0,1][0,1], using the oscillation at the points xk=2/((2k+1)π)x_k = \sqrt{2/((2k+1)\pi)}xk​=2/((2k+1)π)​. (b) Show each gng_ngn​ is of bounded variation on [0,1][0,1][0,1] and gn→gg_n \to ggn​→g uniformly.

xk=1π/2+kπ,g(xk)=(−1)k 2(2k+1)πx_k = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi/2 + k\pi}},\qquad g(x_k) = (-1)^k\,\frac{2}{(2k+1)\pi}xk​=π/2+kπ​1​,g(xk​)=(−1)k(2k+1)π2​
∑k=1N∣g(xk−1)−g(xk)∣=2π∑k=1N(12k−1+12k+1)→∞\sum_{k=1}^{N}\lvert g(x_{k-1}) - g(x_k) \rvert = \frac{2}{\pi}\sum_{k=1}^{N}\left(\frac{1}{2k-1} + \frac{1}{2k+1}\right) \to \inftyk=1∑N​∣g(xk−1​)−g(xk​)∣=π2​k=1∑N​(2k−11​+2k+11​)→∞
Verdict

The claim is false — each gng_ngn​ is of bounded variation and gn→gg_n \to ggn​→g uniformly, but the limit ggg is not of bounded variation.

  • Functions of Bounded Variation
Show solution

Counterexample and verification

  1. (a) Put xk=1π/2+kπx_k = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\pi/2 + k\pi}}xk​=π/2+kπ​1​; then xk↓0x_k \downarrow 0xk​↓0 and sin⁡(1/xk2)=sin⁡(π/2+kπ)=(−1)k\sin(1/x_k^2) = \sin(\pi/2 + k\pi) = (-1)^ksin(1/xk2​)=sin(π/2+kπ)=(−1)k, so g(xk)=(−1)kxk2=(−1)k 2(2k+1)πg(x_k) = (-1)^k x_k^2 = (-1)^k\,\dfrac{2}{(2k+1)\pi}g(xk​)=(−1)kxk2​=(−1)k(2k+1)π2​. Also x0=2/π≈0.798<1x_0 = \sqrt{2/\pi} \approx 0.798 < 1x0​=2/π​≈0.798<1.

    On the partition 0<xN<xN−1<⋯<x1<x0<10 < x_N < x_{N-1} < \cdots < x_1 < x_0 < 10<xN​<xN−1​<⋯<x1​<x0​<1, consecutive values have opposite signs, so \[\lvert g(x_{k-1}) - g(x_k) \rvert = \frac{2}{\pi}\left(\frac{1}{2k-1} + \frac{1}{2k+1}\right) \qquad (k = 1, \dots, N).\] Hence the variation sum over this partition is 2π∑k=1N(12k−1+12k+1)≥2π∑k=1N12k+1≥1π∑k=1N1k+1→∞\dfrac{2}{\pi}\sum_{k=1}^{N}\left(\dfrac{1}{2k-1} + \dfrac{1}{2k+1}\right) \ge \dfrac{2}{\pi}\sum_{k=1}^{N}\dfrac{1}{2k+1} \ge \dfrac{1}{\pi}\sum_{k=1}^{N}\dfrac{1}{k+1} \to \inftyπ2​∑k=1N​(2k−11​+2k+11​)≥π2​∑k=1N​2k+11​≥π1​∑k=1N​k+11​→∞ as N→∞N \to \inftyN→∞ (harmonic series). The total variation is infinite, so ggg is not of bounded variation.

  2. (b) gng_ngn​ is continuous at x=1/nx = 1/nx=1/n (both sides equal g(1/n)g(1/n)g(1/n)). It is constant, hence BV, on [0,1/n][0, 1/n][0,1/n], and ggg is C1C^1C1, hence BV, on [1/n,1][1/n, 1][1/n,1] (V1/n1(g)≤∫1/n1∣g′∣<∞V_{1/n}^1(g) \le \int_{1/n}^1 \lvert g' \rvert < \inftyV1/n1​(g)≤∫1/n1​∣g′∣<∞ since g′g'g′ is continuous on a compact interval). So each gng_ngn​ is of bounded variation on [0,1][0,1][0,1].

    For uniform convergence: on [1/n,1][1/n, 1][1/n,1], gn=gg_n = ggn​=g, so the difference is 000; on [0,1/n][0, 1/n][0,1/n], ∣gn(x)−g(x)∣=∣g(1/n)−g(x)∣≤∣g(1/n)∣+∣g(x)∣≤1n2+1n2=2n2→0\lvert g_n(x) - g(x) \rvert = \lvert g(1/n) - g(x) \rvert \le \lvert g(1/n) \rvert + \lvert g(x) \rvert \le \dfrac{1}{n^2} + \dfrac{1}{n^2} = \dfrac{2}{n^2} \to 0∣gn​(x)−g(x)∣=∣g(1/n)−g(x)∣≤∣g(1/n)∣+∣g(x)∣≤n21​+n21​=n22​→0 (using ∣g(t)∣≤t2\lvert g(t) \rvert \le t^2∣g(t)∣≤t2). Thus ∥gn−g∥∞→0\lVert g_n - g \rVert_\infty \to 0∥gn​−g∥∞​→0.

  3. Conclusion: each gng_ngn​ is of bounded variation and gn→gg_n \to ggn​→g uniformly, but the limit ggg is not of bounded variation. Uniform limits preserve continuity but not bounded variation — variation can "leak out" in the limit.
